subject: publish-policy
detail: A holds every new post as pending until a moderator publishes it; B publishes every post immediately. B's existing posts were never moderated.
solutions: Pre-moderate every new post; migrate B's existing posts as published (grandfathered)
Pre-moderate every new post and push B's existing posts into the moderation queue
Publish immediately and moderate afterwards (drops A's rule)
recommended: Pre-moderate every new post; migrate B's existing posts as published, since they are already public

subject: max-post-length
detail: A limits a post body to 5000 characters (constant and DB check); B allows 10000. B posts between 5001 and 10000 characters would be rejected by A's constraint during migration.
solutions: Unified limit 10000 (widen A's check; no existing post rejected)
Unified limit 5000 and truncate or reject longer B posts (data loss)
5000 for new posts, longer legacy posts allowed through a legacy flag
recommended: Unified limit 10000: widening loses nothing and moderators review every new post anyway

subject: post.author_id
detail: A requires an author (author_id not null); B allows null author_id for anonymous posts. Anonymous posting (M08) was dropped, but B's existing anonymous posts still have no author.
solutions: Assign legacy anonymous posts to one reserved, sign-in-disabled system account and keep author_id not null
Make author_id nullable for legacy rows only
Do not migrate anonymous posts (data loss)
recommended: Reserved system account 'Anonymous (OpenForum archive)' with sign-in disabled; author_id stays not null

subject: user-accounts
detail: B's users (integer ids, 'name', roles user/admin) author B's posts and must be merged into A's users (uuid, 'display_name', roles member/moderator). The same email may exist in both apps. Password hashing in both sources is unknown, so B's stored credentials may not verify in the unified app.
solutions: Re-key B users to uuid with legacy_id; name -> display_name; link accounts with the same email into A's record; force a password reset where hashes cannot be verified
Keep B users as separate accounts even when emails match (email must stay unique, so this fails)
recommended: Re-key with legacy_id, map name to display_name, merge same-email accounts into A's record, and require a password reset for B accounts whose hash format is not supported

subject: b-token-signing-key
detail: B signs JWTs with a hard-coded literal key and no expiry. B's token sign-in was dropped; any B tokens in the wild must stop working.
solutions: Do not reuse B's token code; B tokens become invalid at cut-over
Keep a temporary token bridge (would keep the weak key alive)
recommended: No reuse of B's token code; B tokens are invalid after cut-over; the unified session secret comes only from configuration
